Senses.PreferredTarget: to strike the staff on the floor
Senses.Explanation: Literally, to strike or plant (卓) the staff (拄杖): "to strike the staff on the floor." The phrase occurs 5,243 times in 287 allowlisted texts. In the Chan record it is a teaching-seat action, not merely a description of walking with a stick. A master strikes once and says, "all at once, smashed to pieces" (卓拄杖一下，云：一時粉碎), or strikes and supplies the demanded phrase. The action can punctuate a public exchange, accompany a shout, or close a formal address immediately before "stepped down" (下座). The corpus counts the blows explicitly: "once" occurs 777 times and "three times" 32 times. These observable placements are the Chan deviation; the entry assigns no unstated meaning to the blow.
Senses.Note: The phrase is a stock stage direction in recorded public addresses. It describes contact of the staff with the floor or platform; it is distinct from raising, pointing with, or throwing the staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 卓拄杖一下，云：一時粉碎。又卓拄杖一下，云：話在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the record of Xuzhou Pudu: "he struck the staff once and said, 'all at once, smashed to pieces'; he struck it once again and said, 'the words remain.'"

Occurrences.Kwic: 師卓拄杖一下。僧曰：答即便答，又卓個甚麼？師曰：百雜碎。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public exchange: the master strikes once; the monk asks why he struck instead of answering; the master says, "smashed into a hundred pieces."

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道晝行夜臥一句作麼生道？良久，以拄杖卓一下，云：德山證明。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After demanding, "how do you say the phrase 'walking by day and lying down at night'?" the speaker pauses, strikes once with the staff, and says, "Deshan bears witness."

Occurrences.Kwic: 良久曰。水流千派月。山鎖一磎雲。卓拄杖下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A pause and verse are followed by striking the staff and stepping down, anchoring the closing-stage-direction use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 卓拄杖，喝一喝，便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The record sequences three formal actions: strike the staff, give a shout, and immediately step down.

Occurrences.Kwic: 卓拄杖三下，云：「從來古路如弦直，著腳何非化國民？」下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker strikes the staff three times, gives a verse, and steps down; this anchors explicit counting beyond the common single strike.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道如何是此事？聽山僧拄杖子與你們註解。」卓拄杖兩下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After asking what the matter is, the master tells the assembly to listen to his staff explain it and strikes twice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是蕩蕩無為之句？卓拄杖云：含弘光大，品物咸亨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The staff strike directly introduces the supplied phrase in response to a formal question.

Senses.Explanation: To sit. The compound behaves as an ordinary action verb in Chinese Chan records: someone sits every day in the sutra hall; eighteen people sit silently around a brazier; someone sits with his head covered; and one teacher says he sits amid commotion. The records attach different appraisals to those concrete situations. A teacher warns clear-eyed patched monks not to go sit in the mud. Baichi quotes three kinds of monks in snow—one sitting with his head covered, one sucking a writing brush and composing poetry, and one sitting around the fire talking about food—then calls the first a board-carrying Chan fellow. Qinglong cites people sitting silently around a brazier and sitting with robes over their heads, calls the two earlier speakers a matched pair of frozen fellows, and says his own assembly may sleep or walk: why rigidly insist on sitting? The word itself names sitting; locations, duration, posture, and each speaker's praise or criticism come from the surrounding sentence.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 322 matches in 132 files. 'Sit every day' occurs seven times in seven files; 'sit with the head covered' eighteen times in fifteen; 'sit around a brazier' thirty-five times in twenty-six; and 'sit in the mud' four times in four. The direct nominal form occurs once, in a question about one sitting on Kunlun Mountain. No other required definition formula occurs. The entry therefore uses the plain English action and preserves the corpus's explicit descriptive and critical modifiers rather than introducing a category absent from the Chinese.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔有一僧。在經堂內不看經。每日打坐。藏主曰。何不看經。僧曰。某甲不識字。主曰。何不問人。僧近前。叉手鞠躬曰。這箇是甚麼字。主無對。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A case says that a monk in the sutra hall did not read sutras and sat every day. The librarian asks why he does not read; the monk says he cannot read. Told to ask someone, the monk approaches with folded hands, bows, and asks, 'What character is this?' The librarian has no reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧今日為諸人說破。明眼衲僧莫去泥裡打坐。珍重。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teacher says, 'Today this mountain monk has spoken it through for you. Clear-eyed patched monks, do not go sit in the mud. Take care.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 復舉圓通秀云：「雪中有三種僧：一者、蒙頭打坐，二者、吮筆吟詩，三者、圍爐說食。」師云：「蒙頭打坐，還他擔板禪和；吮筆吟詩，可是嬌兒賣俏。看來惟圍爐說食底在此時較為親切，何故？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baichi quotes Yuantong Xiu: 'In snow there are three kinds of monks: one sits with his head covered; one sucks a writing brush and composes poetry; one sits around the fire talking about food.' Baichi says, 'The head-covered sitting belongs to a board-carrying Chan fellow; brush-sucking poetry is a pampered child showing off. At this time, sitting around the fire talking about food looks comparatively closest. Why?'

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧則不然，青龍今日開爐，親切無如者箇，任從睡臥經行，何必拘拘打坐？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After quoting two winter addresses about silent, head-covered sitting around a brazier, Qinglong says, 'This mountain monk is not like that. Qinglong opens the brazier today; nothing is closer than this. You may sleep, lie down, or walk—why rigidly insist on sitting?'

Occurrences.Kwic: 贏得雙泉，閙中打坐。打坐即不無，且道下水船一曲作麼生唱？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teacher says, 'This leaves Shuangquan sitting amid commotion. The sitting is certainly there; now tell me, how is the song of the downstream boat sung?'

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯有十八高人緘口圍爐打坐。不是規矩嚴難免見諸人話墮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fachang says, 'There are only eighteen lofty people, mouths closed, sitting around the brazier. It is not that the rules are stern and difficult; it avoids seeing you fall into speech.'

Senses.Explanation: (打) to beat / strike / pound + (成) into + (一片) one piece / slab / expanse: 'pounded into a single piece.' In the corpus it is spoken in instructional genres — (開示) ('instructions'), (示眾) ('addresses to the assembly'), (法語) ('teaching words') — and in letters, of a state reached after long unbroken continuity and set against interruption. Zhongfeng Mingben (中峰明本) places it after (乆乆綿密) ('long, long and closely continuous') and against (間斷) ('a break / interruption'): '(纔有此心即間斷矣)' ('the moment such a mind arises it is already interrupted'), then '(自然打成一片)。(直得內心外境當下虛廓)。(彼聖此凡同時超越)' ('it of itself becomes pounded into one piece; then inner mind and outer objects are on the spot emptied out, this-holy and that-ordinary simultaneously passed beyond'). Masters date it in decades — '(老僧四十年方打成一片)' ('only after forty years did this old monk pound it into one piece'; Xiangyan's 香嚴 saying, as recounted in Guting Shanjian's 古庭善堅 record), '(古人四十年打成一片)' ('the ancients took forty years to pound it into one piece') recurs (3 files), and Yulin Tongxiu (玉林通琇) raises '(古人道我數十年打成一片又云我數十年尚有走作)' ('an ancient said, "for decades I pounded it into one piece," and also said, "after decades I still have running-off"'; B27n0152), setting (打成一片) beside (尚有走作) ('still having running-off'). What is said to be pounded into one piece is a range of paired opposites: '(打成一片)，(也無生的心)，(也無滅的心)，(生滅一如)，(動靜無二)' ('pounded into one piece — no arising mind and no perishing mind; arising and perishing one and the same, motion and stillness not two'; Wei'an Deran 唯菴德然, teaching words); '(打成一片)，(情境俱亡)' ('pounded into one piece, subject and object both gone'; Ruibai Mingxue 瑞白明雪); '(佛法世法打成一片)' ('Buddha's teaching and worldly affairs pounded into one piece'; J25nB159); '(地獄天堂打成一片)。(菩提煩惱坐斷兩頭)' ('hell and heaven pounded into one piece; awakening and affliction — both ends cut off'; Zhongfeng Mingben). Tianyin Yuanxiu (天隱圓修) gives it as an instruction: '(十二時中須教打成一片)，(自無不辦之理)' ('throughout the twelve periods of the day you must have it pounded into one piece; then of itself there is nothing that cannot be accomplished'). The variant (打作一片) ('struck into one piece'; 6× in 6 files) carries the same sense — Yulin Tongxiu, in his (工夫說) ('Discourse on Work'): '(所謂行住坐臥動靜閒忙打作一片)' ('what is called walking, standing, sitting, lying, motion and stillness, leisure and busyness struck into one piece'). (打成一片) occurs 311× in 139 allowlist files. The texts assign the word no gloss beyond its literal sense, and neither does this entry. The Blue Cliff Record gives an explicit equivalence: being on 'the one-color side' (一色邊) is 'also called being pounded into one piece' (亦謂之打成一片). Zhongfeng Mingben's Miscellaneous Record supplies a correction to a different equation: if one knows it as 'a silver mountain and iron wall' (銀山鐵壁), 'it cannot be called pounded into one piece' (不可謂之打成一片). These are the texts' own equivalence and rejection; the entry does not reconcile them beyond reporting both.
Senses.Note: A term for a spoken-of state, not a case or an epithet. The texts draw two contrasts around it: (打成一片) ('pounded into one piece' — unbroken, continuous) vs (間斷) ('interruption') and vs (走作) ('running off') — both grep-verified: '(纔有此心即間斷矣)。(乆乆綿密自然打成一片)' ('the moment such a mind arises it is already interrupted; long, long and closely continuous, it of itself becomes pounded into one piece'; B25n0145); '(古人道我數十年打成一片又云我數十年尚有走作)' ('an ancient said, "for decades I pounded it into one piece," and also said, "after decades I still have running-off"'; Yulin Tongxiu 玉林通琇, B27n0152), and Yongquan Jingxin's (湧泉景欣) '(我四十年在裏許)，(尚有走作)' ('forty years I have been in here, and still there is running-off') raised in (三宜盂禪師語錄) (the recorded sayings of Sanyi Yu, J27nB189). Reaching it is dated in decades (四十年 'forty years' / 數十年 'several decades'). The pairs said to be pounded into one piece vary by passage — (動靜) ('motion and stillness'), (生滅) ('arising and perishing'), (內外) (內心外境, 'inner mind and outer objects'), (情境) ('subject and object'), (聖凡) ('holy and ordinary'), (佛法世法) ('Buddha's teaching and worldly affairs'), (地獄天堂) ('hell and heaven') / (菩提煩惱) ('awakening and affliction') — but the frame — long continuity, then the paired terms spoken of as one piece — is constant across houses. Variant graph (打作一片) ('struck into one piece'; 6×) is the same term; do not treat as separate. Attested across Zhongfeng Mingben (中峰明本) (his extensive record 中峰廣錄, B25n0145), Tianyin Yuanxiu (天隱圓修) (his recorded sayings 天隱語錄, J25nB171), Yulin Tongxiu (玉林通琇) (his recorded sayings 玉琳國師語錄, B27n0152), plus Wei'an Deran (唯菴德然) (J25nB154) and Ruibai Mingxue (瑞白明雪) (J26nB188), the last two off-roster so left unattributed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自然打成一片。直得內心外境當下虛廓。彼聖此凡同時超越。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天目中峰廣錄) (the Tianmu Zhongfeng extensive record, B25n0145; Zhongfeng Mingben's 中峰明本 own record), section (示鄭廉訪) ('shown to Surveillance Commissioner Zheng'; cb:mulu). Zhongfeng's own instruction on sustained (參) ('investigation'): the immediately preceding sentence is '(纔有此心即間斷矣)' ('the moment such a mind arises it is already interrupted') — the term is given as the opposite of (間斷) ('interruption'). Own words, not a raised case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 十二時中須教打成一片，自無不辦之理。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天隱和尚語錄) (the recorded sayings of Master Tianyin), section (與吳迪美居士) ('to the layman Wu Dimei'; cb:mulu — a letter). Tianyin Yuanxiu's (天隱圓修) own instruction ('切不可當有當無…這一著子不可放過' — 'you absolutely must not take it as existing or as not existing… this one move must not be let slip'). Own words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打成一片，也無生的心，也無滅的心，生滅一如，動靜無二。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (松隱唯菴然和尚語錄) (the recorded sayings of Wei'an Deran 唯菴德然), section (示生禪人) ('shown to the Chan man Sheng'; cb:mulu). Deran's own instruction, but Deran is not on the roster, so MasterName null. Shows the (生滅) ('arising and perishing') / (動靜) ('motion and stillness') pairing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打成一片，情境俱亡，見色時不知色，聞聲時不知聲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (入就瑞白禪師語錄) (the recorded sayings of Ruibai Mingxue 瑞白明雪), an (上堂) ('ascending the hall' address; head: '可將個本參話頭頓在目前…如雞抱卵、如貓捕鼠' — 'set the head-word you originally investigate before your eyes… like a hen brooding an egg, like a cat stalking a mouse'); his own hall-address words, but Mingxue is not on the roster, so MasterName null. Shows the (情境俱亡) ('subject and object both gone') pairing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 行住坐臥動靜閒忙打作一片
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (普濟玉琳國師語錄) (the recorded sayings of National Teacher Yulin, i.e. Yulin Tongxiu 玉林通琇), (工夫說) ('Discourse on Work'): '(若於行住臥與忙動得力)…(自然得力所謂行住坐臥動靜閒忙打作一片工夫到得一片時節若至其理自彰)' ('if you gain strength in walking, standing, lying and in busyness and motion… you naturally gain strength — what is called walking, standing, sitting, lying, motion and stillness, leisure and busyness struck into one piece; when the work reaches one piece and the season arrives, its principle shows of itself'). The variant graph (打作一片) ('struck into one piece'), Yulin Tongxiu's own treatise. B-canon has no in-line punctuation here, so the KWIC is unpunctuated (verbatim).

Occurrences.Kwic: 老僧四十年方打成一片。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (古庭禪師語錄輯略) (the collected sayings of Guting Shanjian 古庭善堅), section (華嚴大意) ('the general purport of the Huayan'; cb:mulu). A recounted saying: the speaker in Shanjian's recounting is Xiangyan (香嚴) — '(昔香嚴和尚在溈山)…(痛與一劄)，(嚴不知所以)，(于是入南陽卓菴擊竹有省)。(後出世曰)：「(老僧四十年方打成一片)。」' ('formerly Master Xiangyan was at Guishan… [Guishan] gave him a sharp jab; Yan did not know what to make of it, then went to Nanyang, set up a hut, and on striking bamboo had an insight; later, appearing in the world, he said: "only after forty years did this old monk pound it into one piece"') — followed by (趙州和尚二十餘年) ('Master Zhaozhou, twenty-odd years') and (高峰三十年不出死關) ('Gaofeng, thirty years not leaving the death-barrier'). Raised/quoted, so MasterName null. Attests the decades-long dating of the term.

Occurrences.Kwic: 亦謂之普賢境界一色邊事。亦謂之打成一片。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record (碧巖錄) says, 'it is also called the one-color-side affair of Samantabhadra's sphere; it is also called being pounded into one piece' (亦謂之普賢境界一色邊事。亦謂之打成一片).

Occurrences.Kwic: 既知是銀山鐵壁，即不可謂之打成一片。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben's Miscellaneous Record (天目明本禪師雜錄): 'once it is known as a silver mountain and iron wall, it cannot be called pounded into one piece' (既知是銀山鐵壁，即不可謂之打成一片).
